c1-1-001.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | The new committee is consisting of five senior managers.

key.correct: The new committee is consisting of five senior managers.
wrong: We're really loving the new office, especially the view.
You're being very quiet today. Is anything wrong?
This old farmhouse belongs to my grandmother.

item.why: *consist of* describes what something is made of, a permanent state: it is not used in the continuous (*consists of*). *We're loving* (a feeling about something new) and *You're being quiet* (behaviour today) are correct.
item.why_lv: *consist of* apraksta, no kā kaut kas sastāv: tas ir pastāvīgs stāvoklis, tāpēc ilgstošo formu nelieto (*consists of*). *We're loving* (sajūta par kaut ko *jaunu*) un *You're being quiet* (uzvedība šodien) ir *pareizi*.
item.correct: The new committee is consisting of five senior managers.
wrong: We're really loving the new office, especially the view.
You're being very quiet today. Is anything wrong?
This old farmhouse belongs to my grandmother.

c1-1-002.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | Write one word in each gap: Why ___ you ___ so difficult about this? It's only a small change. |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: Why ___ you ___ so difficult about this? It's only a small change.
item.why: *be* in the continuous (*are being*) describes how someone is behaving now, not what they are like: *Why are you being so difficult?* = why are you acting like this?
item.why_lv: *be* ilgstošajā formā (*are being*) apraksta, kā kāds *uzvedas* tagad, nevis kāds viņš ir: *Why are you being so difficult?* = kāpēc *tu* tagad tā *uzvedies*?

c1-1-003.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Choose the correct option: This flat ___ to my aunt, so we only pay a small rent. | belongs

wrong: is belonging
is belonged
belong

item.q: Choose the correct option: This flat ___ to my aunt, so we only pay a small rent.
item.why: *belong to* is a permanent state (who it is owned by): present simple, *belongs*. It is not used in the continuous or the passive.
item.why_lv: *belong to* ir pastāvīgs stāvoklis (*kam* tas pieder): Present Simple, *belongs*. Ilgstošo formu un ciešamo kārtu nelieto.
wrong: is belonging
is belonged
belong

c1-1-004.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | My parents are owning two flats in the centre of Riga.

key.correct: My parents are owning two flats in the centre of Riga.
wrong: She's being very generous with her time this week.
I believe the conference starts at ten.
We're really enjoying the course so far.

item.why: *own* is a state verb (possession): *My parents own two flats*. *She's being generous* is correct: behaviour this week.
item.why_lv: *own* ir stāvokļa darbības vārds (piederība): *My parents own two flats.* *Tulkojot burtiski mani* vecāki pašlaik pieder, *gribas* lietot ilgstošo formu, bet angliski saka *own*. *She's being generous* ir *pareizi*: uzvedība šonedēļ.
item.correct: My parents are owning two flats in the centre of Riga.
wrong: She's being very generous with her time this week.
I believe the conference starts at ten.
We're really enjoying the course so far.

c1-1-005.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Choose the correct option: I ___ with almost everything you said in your email. | agree

wrong: am agree
am agreeing
agreeing

item.q: Choose the correct option: I ___ with almost everything you said in your email.
item.why: *agree* is a state of mind: present simple, *I agree*. *I am agree* mixes *be* with the verb; *I'm agreeing* is not used.
item.why_lv: *agree* ir domāšanas stāvoklis: Present Simple, *I agree.* *Tulkojot burtiski* es *esmu* vienisprātis, iznāk *I am agree*, bet angliski *agree* ir darbības vārds: *I agree.*
wrong: am agree
am agreeing
agreeing

c1-1-006.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | I'm preferring tea to coffee these days.

key.correct: I'm preferring tea to coffee these days.
wrong: I'm finding the new software surprisingly easy to use.
We're beginning to regret buying such a big car.
She's realising how much work the move involves.

item.why: *prefer* stays in the present simple, even with *these days*: *I prefer tea to coffee these days*. *find*, *regret* and *realise* can be continuous for a feeling or thought that is new or growing.
item.why_lv: *prefer* paliek Present Simple arī ar *these days*: *I prefer tea to coffee these days.* *find, regret* un *realise* var būt ilgstošajā formā, ja *doma* vai sajūta ir *jauna* vai *pieaug*.
item.correct: I'm preferring tea to coffee these days.
wrong: I'm finding the new software surprisingly easy to use.
We're beginning to regret buying such a big car.
She's realising how much work the move involves.

c1-1-007.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | Sorry, I ___ ___ what you mean. Could you explain it again? |

item.q: Sorry, I ___ ___ what you mean. Could you explain it again?
item.why: *understand* is a state of mind: *I don't understand*. Not *I'm not understanding* or *I am understanding*.
item.why_lv: *understand* ir domāšanas stāvoklis: *I don't understand.* Ne *I'm not understanding*, ne *I am understanding.*

c1-1-008.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | My grandmother ___ every word you say, but she can't answer in English. (understand) |

item.q: My grandmother ___ every word you say, but she can't answer in English. (understand)
item.why: *understand* is a state: present simple, *understands*, not *is understanding*.
item.why_lv: *understand* ir stāvoklis: Present Simple, *understands*, nevis *is understanding*.

c1-1-009.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | order | Put the words in order. | my flatmate is always losing his keys

key.sentence: my flatmate is always losing his keys

item.why: *always* goes between *is* and the *-ing* form: *is always losing*. With the continuous it shows that something happens again and again, often with irritation.
item.why_lv: *always* stāv starp *is* un *-ing* formu: *is always losing*. Ar ilgstošo formu tas rāda, ka kaut kas notiek *atkal* un *atkal*, bieži ar *nepatiku*.
item.sentence: my flatmate is always losing his keys
answers: my flatmate is always losing his keys

c1-1-010.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | gap | Don't call us at seven: we ___ usually ___ the children to bed then. (put) |

item.q: Don't call us at seven: we ___ usually ___ the children to bed then. (put)
item.why: *usually* + present continuous: a routine that is in progress at that time (*we are usually putting them to bed then*).
item.why_lv: *usually* + Present Continuous: *ierasta* darbība, kas tajā laikā jau notiek (*we are usually putting them to bed then*).

c1-1-011.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | She is always forget her password at work.

key.correct: She is always forget her password at work.
wrong: He's constantly interrupting me in meetings.
We usually have dinner at about seven.
My boss is forever changing the deadlines.

item.why: After *is always*, the *-ing* form: *She is always forgetting her password* (or *She always forgets*).
item.why_lv: Aiz *is always* lieto *-ing* formu: *She is always forgetting her password* (vai *She always forgets*).
item.correct: She is always forget her password at work.
wrong: He's constantly interrupting me in meetings.
We usually have dinner at about seven.
My boss is forever changing the deadlines.

c1-1-012.gate_key: narrative_b2 | B2.2 | text | Say it as a complaint with *forever*: My brother leaves his shoes in the hall. |

accepted: My brother is forever leaving his shoes in the hall.
My brother's forever leaving his shoes in the hall.

item.q: Say it as a complaint with *forever*: My brother leaves his shoes in the hall.
item.why: *is forever* + *-ing* shows annoyance at something that happens again and again: *He is forever leaving his shoes in the hall.*
item.why_lv: *is forever + -ing izsaka nepatiku* par to, kas notiek *atkal* un *atkal*: *He is forever leaving his shoes in the hall.*
answers: My brother is forever leaving his shoes in the hall.
My brother's forever leaving his shoes in the hall.
